 Opinion 
 Upgrading Public Service
 Tracy Cabrera November 16, 2026 November 16, 2026 0 6 mins 
 Public service must be more than doing a job efficiently and honestly. It must be a complete dedication to the people and to the nation.
                              — Former United States senator Margaret Chase Smith
 Here in the Philippines, it’s common to see people lining up in government agencies (and even more particularly in public hospitals), queueing to transact their business and most going tired and flabbergasted because of unfinished business.
 I myself have experienced such. We guess this is a accepted normal in our lives as the poor and under privileged areoften treated as inconviences by most of those behind the desks, though, they are there to delivery public service.
 One way of addressing this is to digitalize services. Through modern technology, it is hoped that the public easier access and easier processing.
 And this is where the Social Security System (SSS) is looking into to improve its service by void the hardship of long lines of people awaiting to be served and provided with what they need from the government mandated to prioritize the welfare of its constituents.
 At most SSS branches, about 60 percent of people lining up are those  seeking to update their personal information, making the process one of the agency’s biggest service-delivery concerns.
 To address this concern, SSS president and chief-executive-officer Victor Alfonso Limlingan told is now working to link its database with the Philippine Identification System (PhilSys) by next month. The goal here is to make it easier for its over 40 million members to update their personal information, particularly their email addresses and mobile phone numbers.
 According to Limlingan, who just took over recently as the agency’s top executive, the planned integration would allow the SSS to verify members’ identities through the national ID system and simplify the updating of membership records.
 He announced: “(We are) working to address the problem by making identity verification more convenient while maintaining safeguards against unauthorized access and online fraud.”
 “Hopefully by December, we’re tying up with the national ID so, we can verify (every member’s) identity,” he added.
 The state pension fund is also exploring arrangements with its partner banks to facilitate the transfer of updated member information to the SSS database.
 Limlingan asderted that the initiative was part of a broader effort to improve the agency’s digital services, including its website, online portal and mobile application.
 He acknowledged that updating member information must be made easier but cautioned against removing security requirements that protect accounts from hacking, identity theft and scams.
 “Any system improvement must take into account the needs and vulnerabilities of its entire membership, particularly senior citizens who may be more susceptible to fraudulent messages,” Limlingan noted.
 The SSS chief executive likewise said the agency was considering managed services and outsourcing some information technology (IT) functions to address difficulties in recruiting qualified IT personnel at government salary levels.
 With this in place, we are optimistic that processing will be upgraded and the public will be given the accessible service it deserves.
